title: The scheme theoretic image of a product of quasi-compact morphisms is the product of the scheme theoretic images
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For quasi-compact morphisms f: A to X and g: B to Y over a field k, the lemma shows that the scheme theoretic image of f times g is the product of the scheme theoretic images of f and g (statement lines 4480-4488). One inclusion is immediate from the universal property: the product morphism factors through Z times Z', so the scheme theoretic image W is contained in it (proof lines 4490-4494). The reverse inclusion is reduced to the affine case in two steps: scheme theoretic images are local on affine opens, so it suffices to treat X and Y affine, and quasi-compactness of f and g writes A and B as finite unions of affines, which may be replaced by their coproducts so that A and B are affine too (proof lines 4496-4507). In the affine case the three images are cut out by the kernels of the corresponding restriction maps on global functions, and the assertion follows from the identification of the global functions of A times_k B with the tensor product of the two coordinate rings (proof lines 4508-4517). The claim is H2: one universal-property inclusion and a localization-to-affine reduction, with the tensor product identification as the closing step.
